canonical_name: python-sgp4 2.23 -- Vallado's SGP4/SDP4 satellite propagator (C++ core + Python), with the official test vectors (Brandon Rhodes)
lineage: Simplified General Perturbations model 4 (Hoots & Roehrich, Spacetrack Report #3, 1980) as revised by Vallado, Crawford, Hujsak & Kelso (AIAA 2006-6753) -- the propagator behind every Two-Line Element set. Orbital mechanics under Earth oblateness, drag and lunar-solar resonance; the package embeds Vallado's C++ and ships tcppver.out, the reference trajectories every implementation must reproduce.

source_identity.sdist: PyPI sgp4 2.23 (the author's release artifact; GitHub tags stop at v2.14)

dependencies: a C++ compiler for the accelerator (pure-python fallback exists)
entry_points: sgp4.api.Satrec.twoline2rv(l1, l2).sgp4(jd, fr) -> (e, r, v); sgp4/tests.py against tcppver.out

example.output: positions/velocities matching tcppver.out to 1e-6 km (ORACLE-backed); the test suite's count

upstream_docs: Vallado, Crawford, Hujsak, Kelso, Revisiting Spacetrack Report #3, AIAA 2006-6753

human_capability_summary.built_to: predict where a satellite will be from a compact element set, fast enough for thousands of objects, accurately enough to point an antenna
human_capability_summary.pressure: Earth oblateness, atmospheric drag, deep-space resonances; a legacy element format whose meaning is defined by this very algorithm
human_capability_summary.success_means: trajectories reproduce the reference vectors to the published tolerance

human_environmental_pressure: perturbations (drag, oblateness), precision, compatibility with a 1980 data format
human_failure_condition: a term or unit slip puts the predicted position kilometres off and the antenna misses
behavioral_entry_point: propagate a deep-space TLE past its resonance epoch and compare SGP4 vs SDP4 branches in tcppver.out

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run python-sgp4-2.23
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: predict where a satellite will be from a compact element set, fast enough for thousands of objects, accurately enough to point an antenna
